detail.title: Physical Mechanisms for Record Robustness
detail.question: What physical mechanisms enable independent observers to agree on a record despite noise, and do these mechanisms differ between quantum and classical systems?

children.title: Robustness and Redundancy in Quantum and Classical Records

detail.title: Robustness and Redundancy in Quantum and Classical Records
detail.summary: Robustness in physical records is achieved when system pointer states are redundantly encoded into environmental degrees of freedom, enabling independent observers to reach consensus. This process, formalizable through Spectrum Broadcast Structures (SBS) and quantum Darwinism, effectively 'broadcasts' information. Furthermore, thermodynamic constraints, specifically the energy cost of erasing information (Landauer's principle), bound the long-term stability of these records in both classical and quantum substrates.
